text:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout v3.6.0 -> metrics alert: p95 +40% (180ms -> 260ms) and inference error-rate spike to 4.8% in us-west-2 canary (slice 2%). Suggest auto-rollback to v3.5.1. NOTE: auto-rollback disabled during change window (22:00-02:00 UTC). Requesting manual decision.

sana: which metrics exactly triggered? token errors or infra timeouts?

deploy-bot: p95 latency and 5xx inference errors. KV-cache miss rate up ~6x. No DB errors. Deploy ID: deploy-2026-03-20-0912.

alex: looks like kv cache compatibility regression from the new kernel path. Quick mitigation: flip kv-compat flag (--kv-compat=false) in canary first. If that reduces errors we can avoid full revert.

katie: CS note — Dedicated customers in us-west may see slight latency blips. If toggle is risky, prefer full rollback and customer comms. Ops, can we open a bridge?

ben: oncall here. I'll run steps. My proposal: try flag toggle, wait 6 min, then full rollback if no clear recovery. I'll open bridge and page CS. :phone:

sana: draft release-note blurb please: "Reverted v3.6.0 canary due to latency and inference errors; investigating kv-cache compatibility. No expected persistent customer impact."

alex: agree with toggle-first. If we don't see p95 drop to <200ms and errors <0.5% in 6m -> rollback.

katie: decision: toggle now, 6m observation window, then rollback if necessary. Ben execute.

ben: Opening bridge #cust-ops-bridge and paging @cs-lead. Executing toggle: `deployctl set-flag inference --name=kv-compat --value=false --env=canary-usw2`

deploy-bot: Flag change accepted. Change pushed to canary 30s ago.

ben: 90s after toggle: p95 190ms, errors 1.1% (was 4.8%). Improvement but still above baseline. Continuing monitor.

sana: :eyes: watching traces, linking logs: https://logs.redwood/ingest/deploy-2026-03-20-0912

ben: 5m mark: p95 185ms, errors 0.9%. Better but not fully recovered (baseline p95 170ms, errors ~0.2%). Alex - your call.

alex: improvement indicates kv-flag helped but residual regressions remain. Recommend full rollback to be safe; we can preserve canary artifacts for root-cause.

katie: thumbs-up from PM. Ben proceed with manual rollback and pin. CS: prepare notify template for customers.

ben: Executing full rollback: `rollout rollback --service=inference --from=v3.6.0 --to=v3.5.1 --stage=canary --force` Then pin traffic back to v3.5.1.

deploy-bot: Rollback job queued, estimated completion ~2m. Rollback run ID: rb-4112345678-a.

ben: Rollback complete. Canary now on v3.5.1. p95 168ms, errors 0.22%. No downstream errors observed.

katie: CS lead (@cs-lead) — please post customer note: "We reverted a recent canary release that introduced increased inference latency and transient errors. We do not expect persistent customer-facing impact. If you saw any anomalies, please reply to this thread and we'll escalate."

cs-lead: Draft posted to #customer-notify and emailed top-10 Dedicated accounts. Included incident link INC-2026-102.

sana: Filing postmortem ticket INC-2026-102 with logs, deploy IDs, and steps taken. Attach perf diffs and KV cache metrics.

ben: Bridge closed, handing off to infra-oncall for root-cause and postmortem. Thanks all. :white_check_mark: 

infra-oncall: Acknowledged. Will look at kernel path and cache serialization differences; will schedule hotfix and follow-up rollback notes.

deploy-bot: Generated rollback runbook and postmortem skeleton: https://runbooks.redwood/rollbacks/rb-4112345678-a
